Which tools let you animate a photo for free?

The clearest published free image-to-video path today is Krea’s free account: you upload a photo, sign in, and generate with the models marked Free plan, using 100 compute units a day and no credit card. Google Flow also officially lets you animate images with frames or ingredients, on the 50 daily credits that come with a Google account. Dreamina has an image-to-video product and says it provides free daily credits, but the I2V FAQ warns that trial or free credits can vary, so this page does not invent a clip count. Everything else is unknown or has no public free plan. For the wider free-tier caps, watermarks, and paid steps, use the free AI video generators guide rather than this page.

How does free image-to-video AI work, and what does this page cover?

Image-to-video AI takes a still photo as the starting picture and generates the frames that follow, usually with a short motion prompt. This guide only lists a tool when an official page says, or clearly shows, that you can start from an image on a free tier. Quality leaderboards such as Artificial Analysis’s image-to-video board are useful for paid-model comparisons; they are not a free-tier allotment. Artificial Analysis AA-Video-I2V v2.1 is a public quality source if you want paid-model Elo; this page does not invent scores and does not rank free tiers by Elo.

    Which free image-to-video option is best for each use?

    If you want a documented free photo-to-video path with no card: Krea Free, using the models marked Free plan, with the unit math above. If you already have a Google account and want official frames-to-video help: Google Flow, at 50 credits a day, with Veo 3.1 Lite at 4, 6, or 8 seconds in 720p, or Omni Flash including a 360p option. If you want Seedance image-to-video in a consumer app: Dreamina may give free or trial credits, but the amount is not a single published figure. If you only care about a watermark-free $0 plan, Pika Free has no watermark and 0 monthly credits, so it is not by itself a source of free I2V clips.

    How do we calculate this?

    Each dollar figure is a current price row, with the vendor page and the date that page was checked. A published rate is a dollars-per-second figure on that page, or an API credit count times the credit price the page states. A credit-plan figure is plan price ÷ credits × credits per clip ÷ seconds, and it assumes every credit you pay for is used. When the vendor marks that count with "~", "roughly", or "estimated", the row is labelled estimated from credit plan and is not a list price. A promo shows its end date when the vendor gave one. The full method is on the about page (https://vidfare.com/about/).
